logline: A morally compromised private investigator in 1930s Depression-era Los Angeles stumbles into a sensational child-murder case that will transform him into the city's most reluctant defense attorney.

renewal.note: Cancelled by HBO in June 2023 after two seasons; co-showrunner Michael Begler confirmed the cancellation, with Season 2 serving as an unplanned finale.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes 75 percent (84 critics); Matthew Rhys's performance and the period atmosphere were the season's strengths; the storytelling was 'somewhat messy' before the finale resolved it.

seasons.review_body: Perry Mason's 2020 reboot transplanted the courtroom procedural to Depression-era Los Angeles and spent its first season more interested in the world it was building than in the case driving it. Matthew Rhys played Mason as a traumatised, mud-caked private investigator - closer to noir antihero than TV lawyer - and the performance held the season together through its plotting difficulties. At 75 percent on Rotten Tomatoes (84 reviews), the season landed with measured approval: the production design, John Lithgow's supporting work, and the 1930s period detail all registered positively. The storytelling was genuinely messy - a child murder case, city corruption, a revivalist church conspiracy, and Mason's own backstory competed for attention without always integrating. The season improved sharply in its final two episodes once the courtroom arrived.

episode_reviews.title: Chapter One
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes 1932 Los Angeles in precise, rain-soaked detail. A murdered infant is the inciting case; Mason is introduced at his lowest point. The atmosphere is thick but the pace is deliberate.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The infant crime scene - the show announces its moral seriousness in a single, unflinching image.

episode_reviews.title: Chapter Eight
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale delivers the courtroom confrontation the preceding seven episodes were building toward. Rhys's courtroom work justifies the long runway the show took to get here.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mason's closing argument - the moment the character finds his voice as a lawyer rather than a brawler.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes 85 percent (31 critics); a more disciplined and cohesive season than the debut, with tighter plotting and a stronger emotional throughline.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 answered the coherence problem of the debut with a more disciplined story structure and an 85-percent Rotten Tomatoes score (31 reviews). A new murder case - a Latino oil heir - gave the show room to engage with the racial and economic stratification of 1930s Los Angeles that Season 1 had approached but not fully excavated. Rhys settled into Perry Mason as a defined character rather than a work-in-progress, and the supporting cast - particularly Paul Drake's expanded role - gave the ensemble greater depth. The cancellation before a planned Season 3 means the series ends unresolved on several fronts, a fact that tempers an otherwise solid finale-season verdict.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 arrives with tighter plotting and a stronger social conscience than Season 1, finally delivering on the city-portrait ambitions the reboot announced from its opening frame.
